title: Cig Kofte
subtitle: Spiced bulgur and tomato paste patties
excerpt: Fine bulgur wheat kneaded with tomato paste, pepper paste, and warming spices into small tender patties. The modern vegan version is deeply savoury and needs no cooking at all.
sourceNotes: Modern Turkish vegan version of cig kofte using fine bulgur and tomato and pepper pastes. Traditional street food, synthesised from multiple Turkish sources.

recipe.batchNotes: Easily doubled or tripled. The mixture keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the mixture a day ahead. The flavour deepens as it rests.

content.text: Cig kofte in the modern street-food version is entirely meat-free. Fine bulgur wheat softens through kneading rather than heat, absorbing tomato paste, spices, and lemon. Knead the mixture thoroughly so the bulgur is fully hydrated and the patties hold their shape.

items.prepNote: Turkish red pepper paste or paprika-hot

content.text: Put the bulgur wheat in the large bowl. Pour over the boiling water. Stir once. Cover with a plate and leave for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add the tomato puree, paprika-hot, paprika-sweet, grated onion, garlic, cumin, salt, and chilli flakes to the warm bulgur. Mix well.
Knead the mixture firmly in the bowl for 10 minutes. Use your hands to squeeze and press the mixture together. It should become smooth and hold together when pressed.
Add the olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, spring onion, and mint. Knead for another 3 minutes to combine. Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Rest the mixture for 15 minutes so the bulgur finishes absorbing the moisture.
Take small handfuls and shape into oval patties by pressing the mixture in your palm. Each patty should be about the size of a large thumb.
Serve on pitta bread or in lettuce leaves with lemon wedges for squeezing over.

items.symptom: The mixture is too wet and does not hold shape.
items.cause: Too much liquid was added, or the bulgur was not a fine grade.
items.fix: Add a little extra bulgur wheat, a tablespoon at a time, and knead it in until the texture firms up.

items.symptom: The patties are dry and crumbly.
items.cause: Not enough liquid or oil, or over-kneaded after adding oil.
items.fix: Add a splash more lemon juice or olive oil and knead briefly. Do not add water.

items.cause: The spices are not enough or the lemon is missing.
items.fix: Taste after resting. Add more paprika-hot, chilli flakes, and a squeeze of lemon until the flavour is sharp and bold.
